studies.Ethnicity Basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
studies.Reference: Alcohol and Dietary Folate Intake and Promoter CpG Island Methylation in Clear-Cell Renal Cell Cancer.
studies.Authors: Schouten LJ, Deckers IA, van den Brandt PA, Baldewijns MM, van Engeland M
studies.Timing: Diet measured at baseline in 1986 with 20.3 years of follow-up
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Diet was measured with a food-frequency questionnaire.

sample_size.excerpt: The Netherlands Cohort Study with a case-cohort design included 120,852 subjects aged 55-69 yr in 1986.

cases.excerpt: Multivariable Cox regression analyses were conducted, stratified according to methylation, including 3980 subcohort members and 297 ccRCC cases.

effect_size.excerpt: Increasing alcohol intake was associated with decreased ccRCC risk, but was not statistically significant; multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for ≥30 g alcohol/day versus 0 g/day was 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.48-1.24], and P-value for trend was 0.46.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Increasing alcohol intake was associated with decreased ccRCC risk, but was not statistically significant; multivariable adjusted hazard ratio (HR) for ≥30 g alcohol/day versus 0 g/day was 0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.48-1.24], and P-value for trend was 0.46.

design.excerpt: The Netherlands Cohort Study with a case-cohort design included 120,852 subjects aged 55-69 yr in 1986.

timing.excerpt: After 20.3 yr of follow-up, paraffin-embedded tumor blocks were collected.
